parents.title: Diaconis-Evans reduces class-function CLTs to weighted trace variance and tail checks

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Trace powers form the natural linear coordinates for conjugation-invariant matrix functions. The Diaconis-Evans triangular-array theorem lifts fixed-mode Gaussian moment matching to a growing linear combination only when two further obligations hold: the weighted total coefficient variance converges, and variance above a cutoff m_n=o(n) vanishes. Thus expanding log characteristic polynomials into Tr(U^j) separates Gaussian behavior of the basis modes from the global danger that coefficient mass escapes to matrix-scale degrees.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes a nonlinear CLT into basis-mode behavior and a precise no-escaping-mass condition rather than inferring growing-mode convergence from fixed moments.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the critic confirmed the triangular-array mechanism and the essential distinction it enforces.

parents.title: Selberg's smoothed explicit formula replaces log zeta by a short prime sum in L2

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The independent-prime picture begins only as a conjectural Euler-product heuristic near the critical axis. Selberg's rigorous replacement starts from a modified logarithmic-derivative explicit formula whose zero sums converge absolutely, integrates it to approximate log zeta by a short prime Dirichlet sum, and proves an L2 error bound. After the divergent normalization that error vanishes in probability, so Slutsky and Cramer-Wold transfer a prime-sum CLT to log zeta without requiring RH or pointwise reconstruction.

parents.title: L2 tail control plus slow torus equidistribution yields a Gaussian prime sum

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The prime analogue of a triangular-array CLT requires three separate controls. Montgomery-Vaughan removes the large-prime tail in L2; an independent-circle model gives a Gaussian limit for the truncated coefficients; and Fourier moment comparison replaces those artificial phases by p^(-i omega t). For the last step, unique factorization bounds every relevant nonzero integer combination of log primes away from exact resonance, while the slow growth of the prime cutoff makes finite-time equidistribution quantitative enough.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates stochastic universality, tail control, and arithmetic equidistribution, showing why fixed-set rational independence alone is insufficient for growing dimension.

Taylor's logarithm identity shows that this sum accumulates logarithmically until either radial damping or angular phase cancellation cuts it off; normalized covariance is therefore the smaller separation exponent, capped at one. Cramer-Wold and Diaconis-Evans then require a separate o(n) trace cutoff so high powers contribute negligible variance.

parents.title: Argument fluctuations turn mesoscopic zero counts into endpoint noise

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Riemann-von Mangoldt expresses a centered zero count on an interval as the difference of log-zeta argument fluctuations at its endpoints. In the mesoscopic limit, the interval-indexed Gaussian is correspondingly D_beta-D_alpha for independent endpoint variables. Its covariance is therefore an incidence rule: a shared endpoint contributes positively when orientations agree, negatively for adjacent intervals where it is subtracted in one and added in the other, and not at all for strict containment with distinct endpoints.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Derives covariance signs from the boundary operator on interval endpoints and separates this mesoscopic law from microscopic spacing statistics.

accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. Finite-dimensional limiting independence is not promoted to finite-height independence of actual counts.

parents.title: Ancestor trees make the minimum covariance positive and constructive

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The interval-min covariance becomes manifestly positive semidefinite when represented by a rooted genealogy. Each variable equals its parent's value plus an independent Gaussian increment whose variance is the increase in height; two variables therefore share exactly the increments on their common ancestral path, so their covariance is the minimum height before the branches separate. Diagonal additions account for independent point-specific variance, and continuity removes the simplifying distinct-height assumption.
